title: The Original Dukke of Death
description:
Get ready for a trip down memory lane.

This positively archeological Berol Prismacolor™ marker illustration depicts my first ever original characters in all their glory.

Holding the Desert Eagle, sporting the double-breasted Armani suit, and posing in front of the red Lamboghini Countach, is none other than Daniel Dukke ( Pronounced "duck" . As you can no doubt guess, this character is the inspiration for my bizarre screen name. )

Daniel Dukke is an independently wealthy, sophisticated jet-setter who travels the world finding evil where he can, and extinguishing its practitioners in the simultaneously coolest and grisliest ways possible.

I never decided whether or not he was a plain-clothes policeman, an undercover detective, a private investigator, a secret agent, or simply an overdressed vigilante, although at one point or another during his existence, he's exhibited signs of being all of the above.

In all honesty, I really didn't care about such particulars so long as the criminal body count was sufficiently high.

As I look at this picture now, the profound impact of the television program Miami Vice™ upon my impressionable young psyche, becomes readily apparent. As I recall, I even owned one of those ridiculous Don Johnson "Pastel Ice Cream Man" suits back when the show aired. (I hope to God no one ever photographed me in that get up. )

Looming large behind Mr. Dukke, is his equally bad ass1 side-kick, Ferdinand Fox, an aspiring crime-fighter who learned martial arts by watching the films of L. Bruce Preslei2 set on fast forward!

Acquiring preternatural fighting skills in this manner, the newly minted Teenage Killing Machine sought out the world's foremost slayer of evil-doers, Mr. Dukke, to learn from him how to become a great adventurer.

When he thinks of it, Daniel will occasionally say something wise and "mentory" to Ferdinand, but for the most part, he just points gifted fighter at the inevitable, incoming cloud of blood-thirsty Ninja Cats and lets him go wild.

Foxes, as it turns out, make excellent human shields.

During my college days, I inflicted the adventures of these characters upon the hapless University of Maryland campus. I probably have a few copies of the collection I made still gathering dust in my attic.

Every now and again, I consider having DD & FF take place in the same "nobody looks twice at a five-foot-two-inch mosuegirl" universe as Most Dangerous Bookstore, and having Daniel be a former associate/ex-boyfriend of Cassandra Cat. In this manner I could explain the bookstore cat's uncanny acumen with dispatching ninja-pirate-zombies.

1.) I made up these characters when I was eight, so it's quite a rush to be able to use the phrase "bad ass" without fear of reprisal.

2.)FYI, L. Bruce Preslei was a recurring character in the strip. He was a rock star who acted in a host of mediocre kung-fu/musicals before disappearing mysteriously in 1975. He is also © John Staton, as are Daniel Dukke, and Ferdinand Fox.

comments.body: Oooh, there was a collection?  I have a few of the strips laying around from when my sister went to UMD.  I simply HAD to save the ones with the Henchbunnies.  I seem to recall Preslei made an appearance and caught a mouthful of exploding bullets.

Yea there was/is a collection. Heh, I totally wasn't expecting to hear any interest at this point. I was all braced to hear how rickety, antiquated, and 80's everything looks here. The next battery of commets will no doubt be along those lines, so for now its good to hear from someone who remembers.Send me a note, let's see what we can do about getting you a copy or two.
Well, yeah, I was kinda saving it as blackmail material. *grin*  I'll send you a note.

The only thing you could possibly blackmail me with would be pictures of me in my old white "Sonny Crockett" suit, complete with sockless deck shoes.Actually, there are probably a great many things one could blackmail me with, but that one sticks out in my mind.Look forward to your note.

You say that now...Maybe someday I'll put up my best Cosplay pic.  I did Russ Post from Those Annoying Post Bros, a comic that I was apparently the only person to read.  Only the second time in my life that I shaved my mustache.
"Human" shield?  Looks more like a walking duck man shield.  Love this drawing

I'm actually quite tickled that you like this antiquated drawing. I don't know why, but I really appreciate it. Thanks.I occasionally think about resurrecting these characters; of course with hilariously superficial changes like giving Daniel a red Ford GT and getting rid of Ferdinand's parachute pants. It's fun to think I might have one or two more stories left in me featuring these two."Human" shield is just a generic term. it would still be Ferdinand charging into the face of all the dangerous, flying objects. Remember Mr. Dukke, the duck, is the smart one.
No!  You MUST keep the parachute pants!  *cough* sorry, I have a not so hidden love for parachute pants You need to carry on with all of your stories, time to start producing them!

You make a great point. It IS high time I do something with all this crap I have sparking between my ears.I guess that's why I appreciate DA so much. Putting out concepts before potential readers in this manner helps convince me they won't be blown off as the ravings of a old nut. But still, I do need to generate the nerve to expose my work to a larger forum.On another matter. I was just remembering how much research I had to do to get the right views of a Countach. When I was mentioning moments ago about giving "Deeds" a new GT, I just "google imaged" more views than my last trip to the library yeilded of Lamborghinis! Times they are a changin.'
DA is also a nice way to upload the first few pages and get some decent feedback from your viewers before taking things to a publisher and having THEM review it a million and one times.

You're strips are hilarious. I loved Mr. Nader and Jennifer. The strip with Mr. Nader with the last panel saying "He's do dense to be guilty" or something like that. I can't remember. Either way I loved them haha

Oh yea, and the law firm run by Gort from "The Day the Earth Stood Still".That reminds me, did you see that super-crappy remake of that movie?  They had Gort turn into friggin nanomachines! Gort! The inspiration for Scott Summers, Cylon Centurions, and the  Knight Two Thousand. Gort, the imposing silver standard against which all killer robots are judged, reduced to a cloud of stoopid nanomachines. I am so glad that movie flopped. There should be a rule, a LAW in Hollywood that states: If you get to a point in your film making career, where you believe a Giant Silver Robot with Laser Beam Eyes isn't enough to hold an audience's interest on its own merits, that you should be ejected from the film industry on the spot!There just aren't enough slaps to go around.End rant. And thanks for remembering.
This certainly takee me back man. I think I'd be interested to see what this duo has to say about our current culture. You know, through guns and violence and such.
Don't forget swords. They'd use swords too. We have to keep in mind their full vocabulary when making statements.
Too True.
soo does he has his own version of Launchpad? (sidekick to Darkwing Duck and pilot for scrooge mcduck)

Sorry no well-meaning, incompetent aviators here. Being a veteran of the New Zealand conflict, Daniel Dukke is an expert fighter ace among his other copious attributes. When the need arises to get around the globe fast, he pilots his privately owned Lockheed YF-12 interceptor (Imagine an SR-71 with weapons.) himself.For the most part Deeds does his own driving and piloting, in spite of the fact that Ferdinand openly covets the driver's seat of Mr. Dukke's insanely cool sports car. Knowing this, Daniel tends to use this fact as a means of behavior modification."Leave a thug alive for questioning, and you get to drive the car."Sadly, Ferdinand rarely gets to drive the car.
Heh I haven't seen this yet.. Looking nice!  Also hows things going on your end?

That's amusing, since the drawing and the characters depicted therein are positively ancient. I should send you the old graphic novel I made with them, although I should warn you, while some of the humor still holds up, I was learning how to draw as I produced it.On the other thing, progress is slower than I'd hoped. My friends tell my I'm being too much of a perfectionist and they're probably right. I think I'll start posting the character design drawings and such here in the gallery to whet people's appetites. I have it so bad that sometimes I never even START a picture because I know I'll just make my self unhappy with what I've drawn.  However at least you have real talent and skill.  The thing with being a perfectionist is just learning the right time to let issues go. That not everyone will see what you see, and the ones that do... Well if you did even a decent job, and not half assed it, you then still did a damn good job because you actuly put effort in to makeing it not half assed.And you and I know alot of art that does look half assed still gets through unfortunetly in comics and those guys still get their check at the end of the month. title: Bunnies for Hire
description:
Now that you've met Daniel Dukke and Ferdinand Fox, let me introduce you to two of their chief villains--The Hench-Bunnies.

This halter-topped and miniskirted pair of miscreants expertly employ all matter of weapons to create mayhem and destruction, sometimes for pay, and sometimes for kicks.

Skilled enough to survive multiple encounters with both the Dukke of Death and the Teenage Killing Machine, The Hench Bunnies present a unique threat due to the usually deadly Ferdinand's critical awkwardness around members of the fairer sex.

One bat of an eye, and the slayer of 1,000 ninjas is out of the fight. It's tragic really.

The Hench Bunnies, as well as Deeds and Ferdy are totally © John H. Staton.
